title: Style Module Imports via Link Elements

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Developers using Declarative Shadow DOM (DSD) do not have a way to share declarative stylesheets without using script. There are many workarounds, but none are ideal.

### What solutions exist today?

If a developer wants to share styles between the light DOM and DSD, they can either:

a. Duplicate individual inline style rules between shadow roots. This is problematic because it often leads to lots of duplicated style definitions, which put pressure on the parser and are un-ergonomic and bloat memory if CSSOM is used to modify their styles.
b. Use classic `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags for shared CSS files in each shadow root. This is problematic because external stylesheets are an asynchronous render-blocking resource, and could cause an FOUC. They are also un-ergonomic and bloat memory if CSSOM is used to modify their styles.
c. Use the Javascript adoptedStyleSheets property on the declarative shadow root to share stylesheets. This is problematic because the shadow root created by Declarative Shadow DOM does not exist until the <template> tag is parsed, resulting in a guaranteed FOUC.

None of these options are ideal.

### How would you solve it?

A variation of `<link rel=stylesheet>` that performs a module import. Instead of the existing 1:1 mapping between `<link>` elements and `CSSStyleSheet` objects, this new link would share the same `CSSStyleSheet` between multiple `<link>` tags.

Proposed syntax:

```
<link rel="stylesheet" type="module" href="foo">
```

`type="module"` would differentiate a module `<link rel="stylesheet">` element from a classic `<link rel="stylesheet">` element. In the above example, "foo" would go through import map processing. The final URL would then be fetched and added to the import map keyed by resolved URL with a type of "style". Subsequent imports that map to the same URL (and have a type of "style") would reuse this entry instead of fetching and creating a new instance.

### Anything else?
